thread:
Sasha: Heads up @here — rolling canary of SDK v9 started ~5m ago. Pager for paging endpoints just lit up, customers seeing page-by-page failures on heavy cursor use. tagging oncall.

Incident Bot: Deploy event: sdk-service v9 -> canary on hosts pool-3 (started 2832104316). Auto-health checks: 2/5 failures on /v1/paged/query.

Kim (oncall-sre): Saw the alerts. Initial symptom: 502s with 'cursor deserialize failed' in api-gateway logs. Repro locally against canary with our internal client test harness.

Marco: Dump from gateway logs: ```
2026-03-15T15:12:04Z api-gw-17 ERROR cursor_deserialize.go:47 "deserialize error" err="invalid cursor format: unexpected token \"_\"" request_id=rid-9a3b
```

Alyssa: Interesting — v9 changed cursor serialization (switched to url-safe base64 + prefix). older clients still send v8 cursors w/o prefix. Looks like runtime tries to decode assuming v9 format and fails.

Priya (eng-lead): So this is an incompatibility in server-side parsing when both v8 and v9 cursors are in rotation. Expected compatibility layer should accept both. Did the canary skip the compatibility shim?

Marco: It did. Canary got the new parsing code but we accidentally toggled the compatibility-accept flag off in the canary config (split config rollout). 

Kim (oncall-sre): Customer impact assessment: we see 0.8% of overall paged requests failing, concentrated on high-throughput customers using cursor-based pagination (listings, large result sets). Latency for successful requests unchanged.

Jules (product-ops): We have three customers who reported errors via support chat (IDs: C-441, C-558, C-772). Escalated to CS. Recommend ASAP messaging for those customers and a public status note if impact grows.

Sasha: Actions: 1) flip kill-switch on v9 canary routing 2) rollback canary hosts to v8 3) open postmortem. Who can flip the flag now?

DevOps Bot: Feature flag controller: current flag: `sdk_v9_enable` = true (canary targets: pool-3).

Kim (oncall-sre): I'll flip the flag and initiate rollback. Command: ```bash
rrctl feature update --name=sdk_v9_enable --target=pool-3 --value=false --reason="paging-serialize-regress"
rrctl deploy rollback --service=sdk-service --to-version=v8 --targets=pool-3
```

Sasha: Please include a short verification plan after rollback.

Kim (oncall-sre): Rolling back now. Patch notes: revert parser change and re-enable compatibility shim. Running smoke against sample cursor set.

Incident Bot: Action taken: feature sdk_v9_enable set to false (by Kim) at 2832104335. Deploy rollback started.

Marco: After rollback, local reproduce shows success. Gateway logs: ```
2026-03-15T15:14:12Z api-gw-03 INFO cursor_deserialize.go:85 "accepted legacy cursor" request_id=rid-1f7c
```

Alyssa: Good. We'll need a quick followup: 1) patch v9 to accept legacy cursors at parse time 2) add unit tests for mixed-cursor scenarios 3) change canary config to never drop compatibility flags.

Priya (eng-lead): Owners: Marco -> parser patch, Alyssa -> tests, Infra -> canary config guard. I want a rollback postmortem doc and timeline.

Jules (product-ops): I'll prepare customer comms for the three impacted accounts and a short status on status.redwood.ai. Suggest messaging: apology, brief cause, mitigation steps, ETA for permanent fix.

Kim (oncall-sre): Rollback completed on pool-3 at 2832104378. Health checks green. Monitoring: failures dropped to baseline.

Sasha: Thanks Kim. Can we mark incident priority: Sev3 (partial customer impact) and assign postmortem?

Priya (eng-lead): Assigned. Postmortem owner: Marco. Target publish in 48h. Include timeline, root cause (config + parsing mismatch), and action items: compatibility tests, canary gating for flags, runbook update (how to flip kill-switch + when to notify CS).

Marco: Will start the postmortem and include reproducer + suggested patch.

Alyssa: Quick note for SDK teams — we'll coordinate a minor SDK v9 client patch to advertise cursor format in requests (opt-in header) so servers can disambiguate during rollout.

Jules (product-ops): Customer comms drafted, will send after final confirmation from Kim.

Incident Bot: Incident closed (temporary mitigation applied, rollback complete). Metadata: impact=partial; customers=3; mitigated_by=rollback+flag_kill; owner=Marco; severity=SEV3.

Sasha: Great job team. Follow-up sync 30m in #incidents-postmortem to draft the PM notes and action owners. :thumbsup:
